research.title: Two small robots, careful steps in the home
research.deck: This week began with Pixel gliding across a kitchen tile, learning from sensorized demonstrations and its own trial runs in ordinary spaces. It shows broad skills for mobile manipulation but there are clear gaps when stairs, touch sensing, or long term planning come into play.
research.summary: This week began with Pixel gliding across a kitchen tile, learning from sensorized demonstrations and its own trial runs in ordinary spaces. It shows broad skills for mobile manipulation but there are clear gaps when stairs, touch sensing, or long term planning come into play. Pixel-UMI adds a layer of safety by relying on scene data and on policy corrections guided by human demonstrations, but it is still limited by a single depth view that can miss hidden surfaces and by approximate contact force signals. The thread here is simple and gentle: affordable robots may take on routine tasks in real spaces, yet reliability and sensing in the shadows remain unsettled, leaving room for careful progress rather than quick leaps.

papers.original_headline: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
papers.headline: Low-cost robot learns tasks but has important limits
papers.deck: An affordable mobile robot and learning tools show what cost-conscious robots can do in everyday spaces, while noting current gaps.
papers.what_happened: Pixel, a cheap mobile robot with simple hardware and learning software, learned mobile manipulation from both sensorized human demonstrations and robot teleoperation. It shows broad skills but has task-based gaps and limits that depend on task and environment in real spaces.
papers.why_it_matters: This suggests cheaper robots can take on many everyday tasks, but safety, reliability, and planning over longer times still need fixes before wide use is possible.
body_paragraphs: Pixel uses a cheap robot and several ways to learn from people and from the robot itself. The goal is to learn safely in normal spaces.
In practice, a business could use cheaper robots for routine tasks, while gaps like stairs, touch sensing, and long-term planning still need work.

papers.original_headline: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
papers.headline: Robots learn obstacle avoidance from human demos, but miss hidden surfaces
papers.deck: A robot learns obstacle avoidance from scene data and demos, but head-mounted depth can miss hidden surfaces.
papers.what_happened: The robot learned from demonstrations recorded with a head-mounted camera. It builds a 3D map from depth data, then retargets human motions to avoid obstacles. The system also masks views that don’t match well, and real-time adjustments helped some tasks.
papers.why_it_matters: This suggests robots can learn safe moves in cluttered spaces from shared sensor data and demos, but sensing gaps and weak force feedback stay risks.
body_paragraphs: Offline scene data help shape the robot’s posture to avoid obstacles while following demonstrations. It relies on one depth view and can miss hidden surfaces.
On-policy corrections add real-world tweaks to the robot’s motions, showing that small human-guided adjustments can improve performance over time without changing the whole task.
papers.limitation: Delay-calibrated action labels are approximate and cannot capture exact contact forces. The offline data uses a single head-mounted depth camera, which may miss occluded or moving surfaces.
